newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Motor racing-Hill qualifies on back row of the grid.
newsitem.headline: Motor racing-Hill qualifies on back row of the grid.

text.p: World drivers champion Damon Hill suffered a humiliating start to his title defence on Saturday when he qualified on the back row of the grid for the season-opening Australian Grand Prix.

The 36-year-Briton, unceremoniously discarded by the Williams team last season, scraped through qualifying after a session beset with gearbox problems in his first competitive outing with his new Arrows team.

His old Williams team-mate, Canadian Jacques Villeneuve, who finished runner-up to Hill in the world title race last year, dominated the session and grabbed pole for Sunday's race with a qualifying lap record.

His new team-mate, Heinz-Harald Frentzen of Germany, joined him on the front row with a last-gasp lap effort in the final minute of the session that proved he has what it is needed to be a replacement for the departed champion Hill.
Double world champion Michael Schumacher of Germany in a Ferrari was third fastest.
Hill, whose victory in Melbourne last year provided the launch pad for his first world title success, finished up 20th after appearing likely to miss out on qualifying until late in the session.
He finally recorded a time below the minimum qualifying time with his penultimate lap of the Albert Park street circuit.
Villeneuve's display meant he had secured pole position in Melbourne for the second year in succession.
Villeneuve, the favourite to succeed Hill as world champion, recorded a blistering time of 1:29.369 -- three seconds faster than his pole lap time last year.
It left him almost two seconds faster than his nearest rival, Frentzen, in another dominating display by Williams, who won the constructors' title last season.
Hill's time of one minute 34.806 seconds was more than five seconds slower than Villeneuve.
